Which Demon Slayer movie became the highest-grossing anime film of all time?
questions.explanation: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Mugen Train (2020) surpassed Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away to become the highest-grossing anime film of all time, earning over 40 billion yen in Japan alone. It follows Tanjiro and his companions on a mission aboard a supernatural train haunted by a powerful demon. Its record-breaking success cemented Demon Slayer's status as a global anime phenomenon.

questions.question: What was the original name of the anime distribution company Funimation when it was founded on May 9, 1994?
questions.explanation: Funimation was founded on May 9, 1994, under the name FUNimation Productions before eventually shortening its branding to simply "Funimation." The company grew to become one of the most prominent North American licensors and distributors of anime, holding rights to major titles like Dragon Ball Z and One Piece.

questions.question: Who founded the anime studio Shaft on September 1, 1975, after previously working at Mushi Production?
questions.explanation: Hiroshi Wakao, a former employee of Osamu Tezuka's legendary Mushi Production, established Shaft on September 1, 1975. Shaft has since become one of anime's most distinctive studios, known for its stylized visuals and acclaimed series such as the Monogatari franchise and Puella Magi Madoka Magica.

questions.question: Which Japanese journalist and Studio Hard founder coined the term 'cosplay' after attending Worldcon in Los Angeles?
questions.explanation: Takahashi Nobuyuki attended the 1984 World Science Fiction Convention (Worldcon) in Los Angeles and was so inspired by the elaborate fan costumes he witnessed that he invented the portmanteau 'cosplay' (from 'costume' and 'play') to describe the phenomenon. He subsequently popularized the term in Japanese anime and manga culture through his reporting. The word has since become a globally recognized concept central to fan culture worldwide.
